newsitem.title: USA: NCAA BASKETBALL-ARIZONA UPSETS NORTH CAROLINA TO REACH CHAMPIONSHIP GAME.
newsitem.headline: NCAA BASKETBALL-ARIZONA UPSETS NORTH CAROLINA TO REACH CHAMPIONSHIP GAME.

text.p: The speedy young Arizona Wildcats continued their giant-killing run through the NCAA men's basketball tournament Saturday with a 66-58 victory over North Carolina to reach Monday's final.

The victory put Arizona, which eliminated top-ranked Kansas to get here, into its first championship game and denied North Carolina coach Dean Smith an opportunity for his third national title and the school's fourth.
Miles Simon, a junior guard and Arizona's only returning starter this season, led the Wildcats with 24 points. Freshman Mike Bibby scored 20 with six three-pointers, five of them in the second half.
"Oh man, nothing like this," Arizona coach Lute Olson exclaimed. "We showed our best."
Vince Carter had 21 points and Antawn Jamison 18 for North Carolina, which shot just 28 percent in the second half and 31 percent for the game.
Arizona shot only 33 percent from the game but was 11-for-29 from three-point range, or 38 percent. The Tar Heels were only 4-for-21, or 19 percent from long range.
The Tar Heels, who came in riding a 16-game win streak, had shot 50 percent or better in 10 of their last 12 games but went cold against Arizona.
Guard Shammond Williams hit his first shot, a three-pointer, but that was all he made, going 1-for-13 from the field including 1-for-8 from three-point range.
"I think the key with Shammond was limiting his touches," said Simon. "We were with him every step of the way."
Meanwhile, Simon and Bibby carried the Wildcats on the offensive end.
"My mentality is, shoot the rock," Bibby said. "I'm going to shoot if I'm oppen. They left me open and I shot it."
"I got open looks," said Simon. "Basically the ball was coming into my hands when I was open."
"When they got open looks, they hit their shots. When the rebounds bounced out, crazy rebounds, they came up with them," said Smith.
Arizona out-rebounded North Carolina 52-48 despite the presence in the middle of 7-foot-3 (2.16 meters) Serge Zwikker for the Tar Heels.
A.J. Bramlett had 10 rebounds, Eugene Edgerson nine and Bibby seven for Arizona while Antawn Jamison had 11 boards, Ademola Ojulaja 10 and Zwikker nine for Carolina.

It was the second time in the tournament Arizona won a clear victory for quickness over height as Bramlett blocked four shots, all in the first half -- the second most in a Final Four game. The Wildcats amassed eight blocks to the Heels' two.
"A very, very big key was the way our interior players played against their interior players. That was very much a key against Kansas as well," said Olson.
Smith also praised Arizona's "excellent job on their interior defence."
"They did a terrific job on the defensive post," said Jamison.
North Carolina broke out first in the game, using an early 12-0 run featuring three alley-oops to go up 15-4.
Olson then adjusted the defence, forcing the Tar Heels into a halfcourt offence, and Arizona, using four three-pointers in a 20-9 run, evened the score at 24 apiece, then took the lead at 26-24.
The Wildcats fell back by 31-26 but scored the last eight points of the first half, capped by Simon's basket on the break and a free throw, to lead 34-31 at the intermission.

In the second half, North Carolina got as close as 38-36 but Bibby hit a 22-foot three-pointer off glass, Simon hit a couple of free throws and, after a long spell of poor shooting by both teams, Bibby hit a side jumper in a 9-2 Arizona run that put the Wildcats up by nine.
Another Bibby trifecta gave Arizona its biggest lead, 15 points, at 61-46 but the Tar Heels pulled as close as six at 64-58 with 52 seconds to go. They never got closer.

Fourth-seeded Arizona was the only team in the Final Four not seeded first in its region but, riding the momentum of its upset of Kansas in the semifinals of the Southeast Regional, now has a chance to win it all Monday night.

"It was beneficial to us to play Kansas, no question about that," said Olson, calling that victory a confidence builder that allowed his players to feel that "if we can beat Kansas there shouldn't be any reason we can't beat any team that we come up against."

Simon, who grew up a North Carolina fan and proudly keeps a kind personal letter of rejection from Smith on his bedroom wall, said: "It feels great to come out and play well in the national semifinals against such a prestigious opponent."

Olson has Arizona in its first final, and told his players not to settle for second-best. "It is the first ever," Olson said. "I told them as long as we've gone this far we may as well get it done on Monday as well."
As the game ended, Simon waved his finger to the crowd and shouted, "One more to go."
